body:
Sure this isn't because there's no `__init__.py` file? Or does a similar
setup on other platforms cause a tidy error message?
Silly me. With and without an `__init__.py` it will crash the same. Original issue updated.
Hate to say it guys, but if you just do a regular install `pip install mypy` you get the same error :(

So `importlib.import_module` cannot find anything in the current directory, even at the entry point. I'm pretty sure this is a setuptools bug, but I'm going to wait till tomorrow when it isn't 4am to triple check :)
Confirmed on Mac. But for a top-level module it still works. What's going on? Did this ever work?
What do you mean by "top-level"? Why would you need to make that distinction?
Yeah, it's definitely install-related -- if I run it as `python3 -m mypy.stubgen pkg` it works.

The difference seems to be that when I run the 'stubgen' script installed in my bin directory, `sys.path` does not include the current directory, while when I just run `python -c mypy.stubgen` it does (the first element of `sys.path` is `''` in that case).

I'm beginning to think that this is actually a feature of setuptools -- stubgen will have to do some work to put the current directory back into `sys.path`. That leads to a fairly straightforward fix I suppose (but I haven't tried making it yet). Also to another workaround: set `PYTHONPATH=.`.

Note that in `--py2` mode a different path is taken that doesn't have this problem.

OK, it's not a *setuptools* feature, it's a *Python* feature. When you run a script, the first item of `sys.path` is the directory containing the script, not the current directory.

It's reasonable, and stubgen will just have to address this.
@gvanrossum , adding `PYTHONPATH=.` isn't a great fix. If you do `stubgen --recursive pkg` it will still break for nested modules...
also, if you try `stubgen .` for a package you're in, you get slapped too
I didn't meant it as a fix, just as a workaround until the code is fixed.

Also @gvanrossum, how did you run `python -c mypy.stubgen`, I get... 
```python -c "import mypy; mypy.stubgen"```

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
AttributeError: module 'mypy' has no attribute 'stubgen'```
You have to do `python -c "from mypy import stubgen"`.

issue.title: Fix stubgen breakage
issue.body:
Add '' back to sys.path when running stubgen

When run as a script, stubgen's sys.path won't contain the current
directory, but stubgen needs to be able to run on modules in the
current directory.

Fixes #4571.
